title: Identifier forms and path arithmetic
description:
Every identifier a domain node carries or names, and the arithmetic between an identifier and the path it sits at. Nothing allocates an identifier and nothing numbers one, so a reference resolves by computation rather than by lookup — which is what makes a disagreement between the two a defect a validator reports rather than a convention a writer is trusted to have followed.

This table is the single home of every pattern that spells a kind. A pattern that spells the kinds cannot be shared across profiles, because the vocabulary is what a profile decides; it is shared across the eight node files of *this* profile, which is exactly what this file is for.

`nodeId` is what `domain-object/1` spells `knowledgeObjectId`. The rename is the vocabulary change this tree applies and the shipped contract has not: composing this tree into the distribution is what carries it across, and it is a breaking change to the frontmatter contract.

slug.description: A name reduced to kebab-case. A name that will not reduce is a refusal rather than a transliteration: stripping an accent takes a rule no specification states, and the same name would reduce differently next time.

stateName.description: A lifecycle state. `terminal` is reserved as a rejection shorthand and is refused as a state name by the validator, which can see the whole state list; the pattern cannot express the reservation.

nodeId.description: Any node of this profile. `dm.<kind>.<scope>.<slug>`, with `subdomain` and `context` taking `dm.<kind>.<slug>` because each is itself a scope.

boundaryId.description: The two scopes a node may belong to: a context is `dm.context.<context>`, an aggregate inside one is `dm.aggregate.<context>.<aggregate>`.

adrId.description: A decision record. Retained for faithfulness to `domain-object/1` and unusable in this network: the framework holds no decision-record node, so every `governed_by` target is a node the base cannot hold. See `x-open` in tables/edges.json.

x-path-arithmetic.description: A path is computable from an identifier and an identifier from a path, with no lookup.

rules.why: each is itself a scope, so it belongs to none
<scope> is the bounded context the node sits in

x-path-arithmetic.lifecycle_slug: a lifecycle takes the slug of its subject
